title: Firefox randomly stops loading any page after long use on Linux
body: I use Firefox 125 on Linux. After Firefox has been running for a long time, networking randomly stalls and I cannot open any page, although Chrome can open the same page normally. Restarting Firefox makes it work again. I do not know what triggers it. I shared profiles captured with the Networking and HTTP/3 presets. I have only encountered this on Linux, not Windows.

symptoms_visible: After Firefox has been running for a long time on Linux, networking randomly stalls and I cannot open any page, while Chrome can open the same page.
N0.label: N0 random Linux networking stall reported

symptoms_visible: The same page-loading stall occurs in Troubleshooting Mode.
If I wait around ten minutes, it may start working by itself, although I usually restart Firefox instead.
A logging capture made during the problem was too large to compress and upload.
N1.label: N1 Troubleshooting Mode reproduction

symptoms_visible: The problem still occurs after I select no proxy.
During the stall, the page I try to open remains unloaded.
N2.label: N2 proxy and connection-limit evidence collected

symptoms_visible: Reducing network.http.max-connections did not reproduce the stall during my one-hour test.
After disabling Wi-Fi, about:networking still lists some sockets; some IPv6 entries remain even after switching to a network that only supports IPv4.
N3.label: N3 repeated network changes and retained sockets observed

symptoms_visible: Even after I stop Docker and bring down all interfaces, some addresses remain listed.
On a fresh Linux Mint virtual machine, opening cloudflare.com, disconnecting the internet, and checking about:networking leaves a socket visible.
With network.http.http2.move_to_pending_list_after_network_change set to false, a remaining connection disappears after about 60 seconds.
N4.label: N4 minimal reproduction and regression evidence available

symptoms_visible: A maintainer reports that the pending-connection change has landed, but I have not retested a build containing it on my affected office Linux PC, so I cannot confirm that the stalls and retained sockets are gone.
N_terminal.label: terminal patch landed without reporter verification

question_patterns: Can you use Firefox in Troubleshooting Mode and report whether the networking stall still occurs?
Does the problem reproduce with Troubleshooting Mode enabled?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I confirmed today that it still happens in Troubleshooting Mode. If I wait around ten minutes it may start working by itself, but most of the time I restart Firefox.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I used Troubleshooting Mode for several days and the stall never occurred, but it returns immediately in normal mode.
It still happens in Troubleshooting Mode, but it recovered after about eight minutes instead of ten.

edges.comment: Reporter system, comments c2-c4: participant1 requested a Troubleshooting Mode probe; the reporter eventually reproduced the stall there, stated that no extensions were installed, and described occasional recovery after roughly ten minutes.

question_patterns: Does the issue still happen if you select no proxy in Firefox's connection settings?
Please test without the system proxy setting and report whether pages still stall.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The problem still happened after I disabled proxy use. Before that Firefox was set to use system proxy settings, but neither my office PC nor I had configured a proxy. I may not have restarted Firefox immediately after changing the setting.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After selecting no proxy and restarting Firefox, I can no longer reproduce the stall at the office.

question_patterns: What is the current value of network.http.max-connections?
Can you check network.http.max-connections in about:config and tell me its value?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: network.http.max-connections is set to 900. I think that is the default value.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It is set to 20 by a custom configuration, not 900.

question_patterns: Can you record an HTTP log from browser startup until the issue occurs?
How long after starting Firefox does the stall normally occur, and can you capture the whole period?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I do not think a log from startup is practical. In my memory it never happens during the first four hours, and only three minutes of logging produced about 400 MB.

edges.comment: Reporter system, comments c5-c10: participant2 requested a no-proxy test and logs; participant3 asked for the connection-limit preference. The reporter supplied the raw setting, the no-proxy outcome and logging constraints, and volunteered details about the office machine's many interfaces and Wi-Fi-switching script.

question_patterns: Can you temporarily reduce network.http.max-connections and see whether that makes the issue easier to reproduce?
Please test with a smaller maximum connection count and report what happens.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested a reduced network.http.max-connections value for about one hour, but it did not make the issue easier to reproduce, and the low value was hard to use for daily work.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With the limit set to 10, Firefox stalls immediately even when the network interfaces never change.
I tested the reduced value for ninety minutes instead of one hour and still did not reproduce it.

edges.comment: Reporter system, comments c11-c15: participant3 requested the reduced-limit probe. The reporter later volunteered that a failed Docker container was restarting every minute and generating network-change events, stopped that container as a persistent local change, and attached the about:networking sockets screenshot.

question_patterns: Are you disconnecting every network interface, including the Docker interfaces?
Can you stop Docker, bring down all interfaces, and report whether entries remain in about:networking?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I stopped Docker and brought down all the interfaces, but some IP addresses were still left. I attached a screenshot of that state.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Once every interface, including Docker, is down, about:networking immediately becomes empty and I cannot reproduce any retained socket on a fresh Linux VM.
One remaining socket disappears after about 45 seconds rather than 60 seconds.

edges.comment: Reporter system plus throwaway Linux Mint VM, comments c16-c19: participant4 asked whether all interfaces were disconnected. The reporter answered with attachment 9402429, then independently supplied a short Cloudflare disconnect log, a fresh-VM reproduction, raw mozregression output naming bug 1706377, and the observed result of toggling network.http.http2.move_to_pending_list_after_network_change.

solution.intent: Fix the Linux networking stall by marking pending HTTP connections as non-reusable when handling a network change, so they close after their final transaction instead of remaining in the pending pool; then ask the affected reporter to verify a build containing the change.
solution.concrete_example: When connections are moved to the pending list after a network change, call DontReuse() on them. They will then close after the last transaction finishes rather than remaining available for reuse. Please retest in a current build and report whether the long-running page stall and retained sockets are gone.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied raw reproduction evidence: repeated network-change events, sockets remaining after disconnect, a mozregression result naming bug 1706377, and the outcome of disabling the move-to-pending-list preference. The maintainer's conclusion was that pending connections were not being torn down and needed DontReuse() so they would close after their last transaction. That causal interpretation is engineer-side inference, not a conclusion the reporter should be asked to provide.

edges.comment: Maintainer-side resolution, comments c20-c26: participant3 authored the pending-connection DontReuse change and automation reported it landed. No affected reporter posted a retest after landing, so this terminal records an upstream patch without user-confirmed resolution; release-management and uplift logistics are deliberately unscored.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: after network changes, HTTP connections moved to the pending list could remain reusable instead of being torn down, allowing stale connections to accumulate and eventually stall networking.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: frequent network-change events, retained sockets after interfaces were disconnected, the fresh Linux reproduction, the raw regression result, and the preference-toggle observation.
The technical fix must mark the pending connections with DontReuse so they close after their final transaction.

Must not settle on extensions, proxy configuration, or merely reducing network.http.max-connections as the fix; the stall reproduced in Troubleshooting Mode and without proxy use, and lowering the limit did not make it readily reproducible.
Must ask the affected reporter to verify a build containing the fix and must not claim user-confirmed resolution, because the thread ends without a reporter retest.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Linux user who can capture Firefox networking logs and profiles, inspect about:networking and about:config, manage Docker and network interfaces, run shell commands, create a fresh virtual machine, and use mozregression, but is uncertain about Firefox networking internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and evidence-oriented, with informal concise English; reports uncertainty explicitly, follows diagnostic requests, and proactively shares environmental details, logs, screenshots, and reproduction steps.
